strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the reopened semantic protocol/event contract blocker with a Runtime-owned generated contract, golden Rust-to-VSIX fixture tests, and guard-enforced drift detection so external controllers can depend on stable request/result semantics.
Keeps protocol semantics, unknown-field rejection, enum handling, and durable event migration coupling inside Runtime/protocol/store authority rather than CLI, VSIX, prose, or model output.
Preserves controlled JSON-RPC and MCP tool execution boundaries by making public Runtime params fail closed on unknown fields while leaving tool execution authority in Rust Runtime.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by expanding the RRP-5 semantic contract from representative methods to every explicit public Runtime JSON-RPC method in the canonical map.
answers.new_capability: The checked-in Runtime semantic protocol contract now covers all 51 explicit Runtime methods, all public Runtime *Params unknown-field policies, and versioned ledger payload shape fingerprints tied to store schema migration policy.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-5.1 covered only representative methods and did not prove semantic request/result coverage for the remaining public Runtime methods or concrete ledger payload shape drift.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless controller could depend on a public Runtime method whose request/result fields were listed in the canonical map but absent from generated semantic compatibility evidence.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-5.2 corrective for full public method coverage and ledger payload shape coupling; it does not repeat RRP-4.1 durable migration recovery, RRP-7.1 terminal/deadline/failure-injection work, RRP-6 module decomposition, or CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-5.2 adds no JSON-RPC method and instead generates/checks semantic evidence for the existing public Runtime methods.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new JSON artifact is release evidence generated by Rust protocol code, not a runtime diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, dashboard, or user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Every public Rust protocol *Params type now uses serde deny_unknown_fields, and task ledger events with payloads carry a versioned payload_envelope for shape/schema migration coupling.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation gets complete machine-checked protocol semantics across the explicit Runtime API set rather than a representative subset.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the reopened protocol-event-canonization gap while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until platform-deadline-durability-hardening, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-5.2 changes guard-engine files, current phase manifest, canonical protocol/event map, Runtime release-readiness audit, Rust protocol/store semantic evidence, and VSIX semantic tests while reclosing protocol-event-canonization. Review must confirm all 51 explicit Runtime methods are contract-covered, all public params fail closed on unknown fields, ledger payload shape changes are migration-coupled, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: docs/architecture/runtime-semantic-protocol-contract.json is generated by brownie-protocol and covers every explicit Runtime method in the canonical map.
Rust tests prove artifact freshness, canonical-map method set equality, all-public-params unknown-field policy evidence, enum values, and fixture serialization semantics.
VSIX tests consume the generated artifact and prove canonical method coverage, validators reject unknown fields, payload envelope fixture evidence, and task.start projection matches Rust wire params.
guard:protocol-event-canonization fails when any explicit method contract, all-public-param deny-unknown evidence, VSIX test evidence, or ledger payload shape migration coupling is removed.
protocol-event-canonization is closed while Runtime Release Ready remains false and platform-deadline-durability-hardening plus runtime-release-guard-ci remain open.

accepted_capability: Rust protocol crate owns and generates the full explicit Runtime semantic protocol contract artifact.
VSIX validates generated golden fixtures, canonical method coverage, and projection semantics against that artifact.
All public Runtime params covered by RRP-5.2 reject unknown fields in Rust and are recorded in generated semantic evidence.
Durable ledger payload shape changes remain coupled to explicit store schema migration policy through payload envelopes and fingerprints.
behavior_evidence: Rust semantic_contract tests cover generator freshness, canonical method-set equality, public-param unknown-field policy, and serde semantics.
VSIX semanticProtocolContract tests cover validators, request projection, canonical coverage, and payload envelope fixture evidence.
guard:protocol-event-canonization and its tests enforce RRP-5.2 evidence through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/protocol/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, queue, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external platform products.
Does not modify .github workflow files; runtime-release-guard-ci remains a separate blocker.
Does not close platform-deadline-durability-hardening cross-platform or Runtime-wide deadline debt.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected docs-only closure because semantic compatibility needs generated fixtures and executable tests.
Rejected VSIX-owned schema generation because Runtime/protocol must own public wire semantics.
Rejected adding new RPCs because the closure concerns existing protocol compatibility.
technical_debt: platform-deadline-durability-hardening remains required-before-release for Runtime-wide persisted deadlines, non-Unix durability, cross-platform process-tree/stale-lock behavior, and the remaining MCP crash-window process-loss evidence called out by review.
runtime-release-guard-ci remains open Runtime-owned debt until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Return to runtime-release-guard-ci only when workflow-scope credentials or an owner-approved equivalent path is available; otherwise continue bounded audits while platform/deadline/cross-platform debt remains explicitly open.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-5.2 recloses protocol-event-canonization with full generated semantic evidence while keeping broader release readiness blocked by platform/deadline/durability and CI release-gate items.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime blockers and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved and more strictly checked.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-5.2.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-5.2.
